comments.text:
Technically speaking, nothing “burns in” on an OLED screen; rather, the pixels burn out.
The problem is maximum brightness. With HDR, this is pushed to the limit in certain spots. The closer pixels are operated near the maximum brightness threshold, the faster they burn out. OLED pixels have, so to speak, an expiration date, which cooling mechanisms attempt to delay. And the mechanisms used for “cleaning/refreshing/whatever” ensure that the pixels under less stress burn out just as severely as the pixels under the most stress. This problem will never be completely eliminated.
In displays with LED backlighting, the backlight breaks down if it is set too bright and gets too hot over a long period of time. With OLED, it is the individual pixels themselves.

comments.text:
I own an 27GS95UE from LG for a year now - I wanted LG's WOLED specifically cause I thought it could be less harmful to burn in, thanks to the additional white pixel (and it also has better peak brightness than QD-OLEDs I think). My monitor now counted around 1300 hours of usage and my experience was great so far - the brightness and overall picture quality is awesome and I can't see any burn-in whatsoever, despite I used this monitor for static apps a lot when I was studying for a state final exam and I also wrote a bachelor's thesis on it. Worth noting is that I use the monitor at 100 % brightness 90 % of the time (mostly set to low peak brightness so it peaks around 600 nits with no ABL) but I also have all OLED care features turned on. So I let system automatically hide taskbar, OLED screen move is set to level 4 and I also let it do automatic Image cleaning function that runs every 4 hours of use. After those 1300 hours I also spotted that monitor did automatic Pixel cleaning feature twice (every 550 hours I guess) that should specifically resolve burn-in problems if any are found. The only downside I had with this monitor at the beginning was an integrated active cooling feature, so you can heard a small fan spinning at the back of the monitor when you are on desktop (while gaming you can't notice that noise whatsoever). However, after that time, even this annoying sound somehow disappeared and I can't hear that noise even when I'm on desktop and put my ear close to the monitor.

So, if you are planning to go OLED in the future and you are worried about burn-in and you know that you'll use this monitor for gaming only, you shouldn't be scared. After the year I also noticed that the monitor somehow gets less warm after a gaming session, despite the overall brightness of the monitor didn't changed. Also, the monitor I own is only a second generation of WOLED panel of this type and the new dual-layer OLEDs that are being released this year are going to be much better in terms of overall performance and burn-in.
